item_argument_dependencies.argument: Define positive analytic finite partition functions, dimension-normalized log pressures, the finite pointwise thermodynamic limit, and the exact local power-series failure criterion.
Define the ACω finite centered Gaussian from an SPD precision, state its normalized density, record the published normalizer/covariance theorem, and fix the zero-dimensional convention.
Construct the finite Fourier basis on the periodic residue lattice, derive the Laplacian symbol, and prove symmetry and positive semidefiniteness including L=1,2 multiplicities.
Prove the chord lower bound, sine upper bound, and global Lipschitz estimate from derivative, parity, range and mean-value prerequisites.
Establish the eliminated principal block SPD and determinant-positive, complete the square, and prove retained Schur positivity including the empty retained block.

Define the periodic positive-mass Gaussian precision, use the Fourier symbol for positivity and the finite Gaussian supplier for normalization/covariance, and cite the massless zero-mode normalizer divergence before specifying mean-zero restriction.
Compare the Fourier denominator to |k|², sum disjoint dyadic cube bounds for d>2 versus d≤2, and use the cited cosine range bound at fixed separation.
Define exact finite Schur updates and determinant log increments over a nested retained-coordinate chain, proving each finite stage is defined and termination.
Integrate each eliminated block by completing the square and translation change of variables, iterate by Tonelli, and identify exact retained marginals and cumulative log normalizers.
Apply the chain rule and ACω change of variables to compactly supported gradient and quartic integrals under dimensionless x=b x′ scaling.
Prove SPD of the star precision, eliminate its center with the exact block theorem, and calculate every distinct-leaf effective off-diagonal as -1.

Show that K=κ(-Δ) annihilates constants and use the volume-preserving split into one constant-shift coordinate and relative coordinates; Tonelli and positivity on a finite box make the full normalizer infinite.

contents.name: §1.2.3 Validity of Mean Field Theory
contents.reason: Mean-field validity requires model-specific fluctuation estimates that this page neither assumes nor proves; its criticality item only defines a thermodynamic nonanalyticity criterion.

contents.name: §2.2.2 The Correlation Function is a Green’s Function
§2.2.3 The Correlation Length
contents.reason: A diverging correlation length is a separate physical criterion; this batch deliberately defines pressure nonanalyticity and proves only a free Gaussian Green-integral estimate.

contents.name: §2.2.4 The Upper Critical Dimension
contents.reason: The interaction upper-critical-dimension argument is distinct from the integrability threshold of the massless Gaussian covariance proved here.

contents.name: §3.1.1 Universality Explained
contents.reason: Universality requires comparison across interacting models, which none of the assigned finite-dimensional Gaussian elimination statements establishes.

contents.name: §3.2.1 Critical Exponents Revisited
contents.reason: The exponent relations require scaling hypotheses about an interacting thermodynamic limit, and the assigned engineering identity makes no such claim.

contents.name: §3.3.1 In the Vicinity of the Fixed Point
contents.reason: The interacting flow near a fixed point is outside the exact finite Gaussian block calculation and the compactly supported scaling identity.

contents.name: §3.3.2 Dangerously Irrelevant
contents.reason: Dangerous irrelevance concerns interacting singular limits and is not implied by the engineering scaling proof on smooth test fields.

contents.name: §3.3.3 Emergence of Rotational Symmetry
contents.reason: Rotational symmetry emergence is a scaling-limit claim; the periodic finite lattice operator retains its explicitly discrete coordinate convention.
